title: Traffic spike on a stateless API
story: 60 users (1 s think time) flood one web replica capped at 0.5 CPU (about 25 req/s). Expected heal: scale out.

timeline.thought: Dry run passed with no violations. Applying the fix now.

args.summary: Scaled web from 1 to 2 replicas to relieve CPU saturation (peak 53% against the 50% per-replica cpu limit) causing request queuing and timeouts (p50 1594ms, max 1800ms vs 800ms threshold); service is stateless and horizontal scaling is permitted.

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: CPU saturation on the single `web` replica — cpu_pct_peak_total hit 53% against the 50%-per-replica cpu limit (cpus: 0.5) right when latency spiked (p50 1594.3ms, max 1800ms vs. the 800ms threshold, with a timeout error and a BrokenPipeError from a client giving up), while memory stayed tiny (20.5MB/128MB) so it's not an OOM issue; each request is CPU-bound (~20ms CPU) so one replica's cpu limit caps throughput.
CHANGE: Scaled `web` from 1 to 2 replicas (memory/cpus unchanged); service is stateless (`stateful: false`) and traefik auto-discovers new replicas, so horizontal scaling is the correct fix for CPU-bound saturation rather than raising cpus (which would still leave a single point of throughput limit) or memory (not the bottleneck).
GUARDRAILS: Within policy — replicas 2 is between min_replicas 1 and max_replicas 3, "scale" is an allowed_action, memory/cpus/image/ports/labels/env left untouched, and the dry-run validate returned ok:true with no violations before apply.
FOLLOW-UP: Monitor probe p50/max over the next verification window (5 consecutive checks, 60s timeout); if CPU still peaks near the per-replica limit under load, consider scaling to 3 replicas or raising cpus toward max_cpus 1.0 next, and log the outcome in the incident ledger.
